old: Methods. Genotypes were obtained from the Pf8 Zarr store over HTTPS, restricted to Ghanaian samples, sites passing the release filter, biallelic single-nucleotide polymorphisms only (the ingest mask is FILTER_PASS & is_snp & numalt == 1), and the GT, AD, DP and GQ fields. Sample quality control applied a within-host fixation index (Fws) threshold of 0.95, a call-rate floor of 0.80, a heterozygosity outlier rule and clonal pruning; mixed calls were resolved to the majority allele by read depth and allele counts taken as one allele per isolate. Variant missingness is now recomputed after the sample cut rather than before it, which yields 3,916 SNPs across 1,900 isolates (mean missingness 2.95%): Guinea savanna 1,334, deciduous forest 337, coastal savanna 204, transitional zone 25. Analyses comprised three ordinations of the published Pf8 genotype-distance matrix (originally computed on the 4,905 release-QC-pass isolates and now re-run on the 1,900-isolate analysis set, by re-slicing the distance submatrix rather than reusing the cached full-set one), pairwise Hudson FST with a block jackknife, ADMIXTURE at K = 1-8 with cross-validation, Mantel tests of isolation by distance at zone and region level with a leave-one-population-out jackknife, TreeMix with 0-5 migration edges and jackknife edge standard errors, and a BayPass XtX scan calibrated against 100,000 pseudo-observed neutral SNPs with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values. Two further checks were added at final revision and both are reported below: a six-scenario threshold sensitivity analysis that rebuilds the analysis matrix under varied Fws and MAF cuts and recomputes pairwise FST and the region-level Mantel test in each, and a call-quality audit of the 19 XtX outliers against the other 3,897 scanned SNPs on the Pf8 annotation fields (MQ, VQSLOD, QD, FS, SOR, ReadPosRankSum, ExcessHet, InbreedingCoeff, culprit, RegionType). The resistance panel is separate and has been rebuilt from the codon up: 57 codons in nine genes were reconstructed from the CDS and the Pf3D7 reference genome - each codon mapped to its three genomic positions, every variant record at those positions collected regardless of numalt or is_snp, each isolate's alleles applied to the reference codon, and the codon translated - so that what is reported is the full residue spectrum including the reference residue, with Wilson confidence intervals and a four-zone chi-square test per residue. Mixed calls make a codon uncalled rather than being assigned a residue. Within-isolate haplotypes were counted on complete cases only; every call was compared one-for-one against MalariaGEN's published genotypes; and the pfk13 list was taken from the WHO compendium of validated and candidate markers, v1.0 (December 2025), rather than written by hand.

old: [Calculated] Principal findings: drug-resistance markers. The previous version's resistance findings were affected by a defect in how markers were identified - the panel matched SnpEff protein-change strings, which can see neither a resistance allele that is itself the reference residue nor a residue that requires two nucleotide changes in one codon - and the panel has been rebuilt by codon reconstruction, which corrects it. And the former "naming discrepancy" at pfcrt 75 was never a naming matter: N75E requires two SNPs in one codon (403621 A>G, annotated Asn75Asp; 403623 T>A, annotated Asn75Lys), and neither annotation names it. Haplotypes are now counted within isolates on complete cases. The pfdhfr IRN triple mutant is 0.771 (n = 1,876; 95% CI 0.751-0.789) - not the marginal range 0.786-0.908 previously quoted, and, as it must be, below its lowest component on the same complete-case set (51I = 0.788); NRN sits at 0.116 and the fully wild-type NCS at 0.091, so it is not a near-fixed single haplotype, and the quadruple IRNL is 0.000. pfcrt CVIET is 0.071 and is demonstrably a single unit: only CVMNK (0.929) and CVIET occur at codons 72-76, with nothing intermediate. pfdhps GE (437G + 540E) is 0.010. old: [Interpreted] Conclusion. At the resolution these data permit, Ghanaian P. falciparum shows no differentiation this design can detect at the retained common variants. That is now the strongest claim this report carries - a statement about measured differentiation, not a demonstration of random mating, for which these data contain no direct evidence. The sensitivity analysis is the reason: the maximum pairwise FST stays within 0.00204-0.00255 across all six threshold scenarios, over 1,900 to 4,403 isolates and 3,275 to 10,876 SNPs, so the headline result is insensitive to both of the cuts that define the dataset. The companion claim does not survive the same treatment. The region-level isolation-by-distance result is significant at the published thresholds and at MAF >= 0.02, but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, and this report therefore no longer asserts a distance effect, weak or otherwise. What remains of the spatial signal is a single south-to-north contrast, visible in the FST ranking and in the K = 2 minor component, with no robust evidence that genetic distance scales with geographic distance. That near-panmixia is a statement about neutral common-variant structure only: neutral common-variant differentiation between zones is negligible, so a spatially sparse design is adequate for characterising neutral structure, but marker-frequency representativeness is a separate question, and the resistance panel in this analysis shows significant between-zone variation at p < 0.001 at pfdhfr, pfdhps and pfaat1. That threshold is stated because it is a selection: on the four-zone chi-square as reported, several further loci are nominally significant at p < 0.05, among them pfcrt I356T (p = 1.6 x 10 to the -3), pfmdr2 I492V (p = 0.020) and pfmdr1 N86Y (p = 0.029). Low neutral FST therefore does not license an assumption that marker frequencies are spatially representative. The pfk13 result is a genuine tested negative - no screened resistance allele occurs at any of the 23 codons, which cover the complete WHO-validated set of 14 and all 6 candidates: twenty-two are fixed at the reference residue and codon 458 is at 0.9995 on a single Asn458Asp call, which is not the validated N458Y, on 1,845 to 1,876 isolates called per codon - rather than an untested absence; it is also a statement about 2009-2021 and not about current parasite populations. The XtX set remains a ranked candidate list, of which 13 SNPs survive FDR 10% and two adjacent chromosome-11 sites - one of them the fifth-ranked SNP overall - are flagged lower confidence on ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff grounds. All zone-level results describe a compound variable in which ecology, administrative region, collection period and sequencing study cannot be separated; that is a property of the Pf8 metadata, not of the analysis.

[Interpreted] Robustness of these conclusions to the corrected re-runs and the final checks. The population-structure readings held on a 16.6% larger SNP panel (3,359 to 3,916 SNPs) with corrected filter ordering, a bitwise-reproducible single-threaded BayPass, seeded permutation tests and full false-discovery accounting: near-panmixia, maximum FST of approximately 0.0023, and a near-flat ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve. Three quantities moved and should not be described as unchanged: the XtX threshold (the manuscript's 8-thread run gave 11.232, the final single-threaded run gives 10.840), the outlier count (15 to 19) and the outlier gene list (11 to 13 genes). One conclusion has since been lost, and it was the report's only positive spatial finding. The threshold sensitivity analysis shows the region-level Mantel result significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, and it also withdraws the earlier claim that the result no longer depends on the censoring of negative FST pairs: of the six scenarios only the baseline clears p < 0.05 both censored and uncensored, the second significant scenario (MAF >= 0.02) giving p = 0.047 censored against p = 0.050 uncensored. Isolation by distance is retained in the report and reported with the scenarios in which it fails, but it is graded not robust, and the previous version's listing of it among the strengthened results is withdrawn. Two strengthenings stand. Near-panmixia is now supported by FST stability across 0.00204-0.00255 over all six scenarios, which is better evidence than any single run could give; and TreeMix decides m = 2 on edge p-values instead of hedging between m = 2 and m = 3. Two further checks changed nothing material. Re-running the three ordinations on the 1,900-isolate analysis set rather than the 4,905 pre-QC isolates leaves the reading intact - silhouette by zone -0.020 against -0.016 on the full set, so removing polyclonal and clonally redundant isolates does not sharpen the structure; trustworthiness 0.499 (UMAP), 0.526 (t-SNE), 0.510 (PCoA), PCoA distance correlation 0.287 against 0.322 - and the call-quality audit clears the outlier set while downgrading two chromosome-11 SNPs. The resistance panel is a different matter and was not confirmed but replaced: an external critique upheld in full showed that the marker identification method was unsound, and the panel was rebuilt from the codon up, changing the pfdhfr triple-mutant figure, adding a locus that had been missing altogether, correcting a residue call, correcting the pfk13 list, and replacing the validation argument. The population analyses are therefore a partial confirmation with two strengthened results, one lost result, two downgraded outlier SNPs and one materially revised candidate list; the resistance results are new.

old: [Interpreted] Questions 1, 3 and 4 are answerable at the resolution these data permit and are answered in Section 6. Question 1 is answered robustly: the low-differentiation reading survives both threshold relaxations, with max FST between 0.00204 and 0.00255 across the six scenarios. Question 2 is answered negatively. The distance effect it tests is significant at the published thresholds but in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, so the honest answer is that these data do not establish isolation by distance; whether that is a statement about Ghanaian parasite demography or about the fragility of a Mantel test on 21 pairs from 7 coordinates cannot be settled here, and both readings are consistent with everything else in the report. Question 5 is answerable only in the weak sense of producing a ranked candidate list: with four populations and 3,916 SNPs the scan has limited power, 3.9 of the 19 SNPs above the quantile threshold are expected to be false positives, only 13 survive FDR 10%, and two - including the fifth-ranked SNP overall - carry ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signatures that put them at lower confidence. Question 6 is answered directly, by genotyping rather than by scan, which is why a reference-residue frequency at or near 1.000 at a pfk13 codon is now informative where a non-significant XtX value would not have been - subject to two limits that must travel with the number. It is fixation among called genotypes, 1,845 to 1,876 isolates per codon rather than all 1,900, and it describes isolates collected between 2009 and 2021. The corroborating MalariaGEN kelch13 status exists for only 36 of those isolates, because Pf8 treats any missing call across amino acids 349-726 as undetermined, so it is supporting rather than independent evidence.

old: [Interpreted] The practical reading is as follows. Study confounding does not threaten the central negative result, because that result is an absence of differentiation: batch effects, if anything, inflate apparent between-group differences, so a batch-confounded design that still returns FST ≈ 0.002 is reporting an upper bound on true differentiation rather than a false positive. It does threaten any positive between-zone claim — the maximum-FST pair, the polyclonality gradient, the ADMIXTURE minor-component ordering, and the marker-frequency differences in §6.9 — because for the pairs concerned there is no study-level control to appeal to. Each of those claims should be read as "differs between zones, which in these data means between zone, region, period and sequencing batch jointly".

Among the 1,900 analysis isolates, six non-reference calls are sourced from those 29 records, at three positions, and all three are in pfk13 at WHO-validated marker codons: 1,724,975 (codon 675, A675V) with four carriers, 1,725,315 (codon 561, R561H) with one, and 1,725,339 (codon 553, P553L) with one. None of the six changes a reported residue, for two separable reasons. At codons 561 and 553 every alternative allele at the failing position is synonymous — the reference codons are CGT and CCG, and the ALTs give CGG, CGC, CGA and CCA, CCT, which still encode Arg and Pro — so the one homozygous call among the six, isolate SPT19969 at codon 561, correctly counts as Arg561 and the reported 1,864 of 1,864 is right. At codon 675 the alternative is non-synonymous but encodes Pro, not the validated Val, and all four carriers are heterozygous, so the mixed-call rule made the codon uncalled for them. No screened WHO resistance residue is produced by any filter-failing record, and the tested negative therefore stands. One consequence should still travel with the number: those four codon-675 carriers have well-supported minor alleles — 22% to 28% of 173 to 435 reads at GQ 99 — so codon 675's denominator of 1,845 is the lowest in the panel, and its exclusions are not random with respect to genotype.

[Observed] The reconstruction has a bounded input domain, and the bound was not previously stated. A variant record whose ALT differs in length from its REF is skipped by a continue, but the isolate carrying it is not marked uncalled, so in principle it would be reported with the reference-derived residue. Three further limits travel with that one. The spanning-deletion allele is written “*” and has length one, so where REF is a single base it passes the length test rather than failing it, and is substituted into the codon as though it were a nucleotide, yielding the sentinel residue X rather than a silent reference call. An equal-length multi-base record contributes only its first base. And records are retrieved by anchor position, so a record anchored outside the panel whose REF span covers a codon position is never fetched at all. Absence of a variant record is likewise read as the reference base.

[Observed] Those conditions occur in this panel, and they change nothing in it. Of the 125 variant records sitting exactly at the 171 panel positions, 16 carry at least one length-changing ALT and 2 have a multi-base REF; a further 19 records anchored outside the panel have a REF span covering a panel position. Genotypes were retrieved for all 32 affected records across all 1,900 isolates. Three have any homozygous non-reference carrier: pfcrt codon 76 with 133, pfcrt codon 271 with 138, and pfdhps codon 431 with 26. In every case the carriers sit on a supported, equal-length allele — codon 76 on ALT1 C, with none on the 55-base insertion; codon 271 on ALT1 GAACGTAAGA, with none on ALT2, none on the spanning deletion and none on the single-base C; codon 431 on ALT1 G, with none on the spanning deletion and none on the 20-base insertion. No isolate anywhere in the panel carries a length-changing allele as a homozygous call, and the 62 mixed calls at these records are removed by the mixed-call rule regardless. The counts reconcile exactly with the reported table: Lys76Thr 133, Gln271Glu 138, Ile431Val 26, and homozygous-reference counts of 1,741 and 1,735 against reported reference-residue counts of 1,741 and 1,735. No residue anywhere in the panel is X, which confirms independently that no spanning-deletion allele was ever substituted. The two multi-base REF records differ from the reference at their first base only, so applying one base loses nothing here. And none of the 57 codons is record-free, so the convention of reading absence as reference never determines a reported residue. The limitation is real and bounds what the implementation may be applied to; on these inputs it moves no published number. What still rests on an assumption is callability: a codon is called when its constituent genotypes are present and unmixed, which is a statement about the genotype array and not an independent measurement of per-isolate coverage.

old: The *kelch13* corroboration is weaker than previously claimed. Pf8 also publishes a kelch13 resistance status, and the previous version leaned on it as independent support for the artemisinin negative. That support must be stated far more weakly. Pf8 assigns the status over the whole 349–726 propeller domain and classifies any missing call in that range as undetermined — "Any missing call in amino acids 349-726 → Missing → Undetermined" — so only 36 isolates carry a complete status. Thirty-six complete statuses are weak corroboration for per-codon calls on roughly 1,860 isolates, and the two are not equivalent evidence. The per-sample concordance above, on 25 markers and 47,012 calls, is the validation that carries weight; the kelch13 status is mentioned for completeness and nothing rests on it.

old: Robustness. The corrected re-run changed the SNP panel by 16.6 per cent, replaced the Mantel significance test, added false-discovery control to the outlier scan and resolved the TreeMix model choice by test rather than by judgement. None of the substantive population-genetic conclusions moved. Pairwise FST remained of order 0.002, the ADMIXTURE cross-validation curve remained nearly flat with a negligible improvement at K = 2 (0.84384 at K = 1 against 0.83925 at K = 2, all eight values on the same 3,385-SNP pruned panel — 0.54 per cent), and near-panmixia continued to hold. That is a robustness result in its own right and is reported as one in Section 6.9. It must not, however, be generalised, and the later threshold sensitivity analysis is why: when the two thresholds that define the dataset were varied rather than the filter order, one conclusion did move, and the isolation-by-distance result lost its support (Section 3.14). The re-run's stability was stability under a correction to how the published thresholds were applied, not stability under a change to the thresholds themselves, and only the second kind of check could have found what the second kind of check found. The marker panel is the third case and should not borrow either reassurance: there, the rebuild changed what is reported, and the honest summary is that four rounds of correction each contained a further defect, every one of them a failure of external correctness that internal consistency checking was never going to catch.

old: Honesty note — the GQ decision is still unvalidated. No direct genotype-concordance check has been run, and the decision therefore rests on indirect evidence throughout. The two specific gaps: (i) the allele-frequency comparison offered in support (0.282 against 0.294) is between two different SNP sets, not the same sites under the two masks, so it does not test whether dropping the GQ rule admits wrong calls — only that the two surviving sets have similar mean frequencies; (ii) no comparison has been made against an independent truth set, although one exists and was used elsewhere in this project. MalariaGEN publishes its own genotype calls for these same 1,900 isolates, and they were used successfully to cross-validate the resistance-marker panel (21 of 23 markers agreeing within 0.03). The equivalent check here — per-call concordance between DP-only and DP+GQ masking at a common set of sites, benchmarked against those published calls — is cheap, is the check the manuscript's own reviewer note asks for first, and has not been done. Until it is, the GQ decision should be read as a power-for-accuracy trade made on plausible but indirect grounds, and the SNP-count gain it produced — 3,359 against 2,143, about 57 per cent, both under the superseded filter order — should be reported as contingent on it.

old: [Calculated] One printed edge p-value is a floating-point artefact, and it is recorded here so that it is not carried forward as a measured quantity. At m = 3 the second edge is reported with jackknife mean 0.829575, standard error 0.0787911 and p < 2.22507 × 10⁻³⁰⁸. That p-value is not consistent with its own mean and standard error: z = 0.829575/0.0787911 = 10.53, whose one-sided normal tail is about 3.2 × 10⁻²⁶, and 2.2250738585072014 × 10⁻³⁰⁸ is exactly DBL_MIN, the smallest normal double-precision float. The figure is TreeMix’s underflow sentinel, not a computed tail probability. Recomputing all six edge p-values from the printed means and standard errors reproduces the other five to three significant figures — at m = 1, z = 7.84 gives 2.20 × 10⁻¹⁵ against the printed 2.22045 × 10⁻¹⁵; at m = 2, z = 3.18 gives 7.48 × 10⁻⁴ against 0.000747653 and z = 8.06 gives 3.80 × 10⁻¹⁶ against 3.33067 × 10⁻¹⁶; at m = 3, z = 3.09 gives 9.91 × 10⁻⁴ against 0.00099053 and z = 0.446 gives 0.328 against 0.327622. Two consequences follow. The reproduction confirms that the final run did compute jackknife standard errors, which an earlier script snapshot lacking the -se flag had put in doubt; and the anomalous value belongs to the rejected m = 3 model, while the two p-values the m = 2 choice rests on are both reproducible, so no reported result depends on it.
new: [Calculated] Two printed edge p-values are floating-point artefacts, three more are visibly imprecise, and a single mechanism accounts for all five. An earlier version of this paragraph said that five of six values reproduced to three significant figures; that was wrong, and the corrected accounting follows. Recomputing every migration-edge p-value in m = 0 to 5 as a one-sided normal tail from the printed jackknife mean and standard error gives fifteen edges, of which thirteen carry a finite printed value and two print “< 2.22507 × 10⁻³⁰⁸”. That figure is exactly DBL_MIN, the smallest normal double-precision float, and it appears at m = 3 edge 2 (z = 10.53, stable tail 3.18 × 10⁻²⁶) and again at m = 4 edge 2 (z = 9.33, stable tail 5.45 × 10⁻²¹). Of the thirteen finite values, ten reproduce to three significant figures. The three that do not are m = 1 edge 1 (0.8% relative error), m = 2 edge 2 (14.2%) and m = 5 edge 2 (3.1%), and all three sit at z ≥ 7.8. The mechanism is computation of the upper tail as 1 − Φ(z) in double precision: near z = 8 the cumulative probability lies within about one unit in the last place of 1, so the subtraction destroys most of the significand. Evaluating 1 − fl(Φ(8.060)) in float64 returns 3.330669 × 10⁻¹⁶, which is the printed m = 2 value to every digit printed, against a true tail of 3.8147 × 10⁻¹⁶; beyond roughly z = 9.4 the same subtraction underflows to exactly zero, which is what produces the two sentinels. The conclusion is accordingly stronger than any count of matching digits. Every printed value, the sentinels included, is reproduced by a normal tail computed from the printed mean and standard error through that formulation — in the m = 2 case to the last printed digit — which a run that had not computed jackknife standard errors could not have produced, resolving a doubt raised by an earlier script snapshot lacking the -se flag. None of it changes a reported result: both sentinels belong to m = 3 and m = 4, neither of which is reported, and the two values the m = 2 choice rests on are 7.48 × 10⁻⁴ and a tail of order 10⁻¹⁶ whose exact digits affect no inference.

old: [Hypothesized] What, then, maintains 0.82 in coastal savanna? Three candidates, and the panel cannot choose between them. (a) Historical persistence. Chloroquine was withdrawn in Ghana two decades ago and the pfcrt CVIET haplotype has reverted to 0.071 (Section 6.9.7), so standing chloroquine pressure cannot explain a frequency of 0.82; but a potentiating variant with a modest fitness cost can decay slowly and unevenly, and a gradient rather than fixation or loss is the expected intermediate state. *(b) Amodiaquine, as an untested possible driver. Ghana's first-line regimen since 2005 has been artesunate–amodiaquine, which maintains continuous 4-aminoquinoline pressure. The published experiment measured amodiaquine and found the shift sub-threshold, and the authors reject the wider-quinoline reading for their Southeast Asian data; so amodiaquine can be offered here only as a possibility that the functional work does not support and did not test in a West African background — not as the explanation, which is how the previous version framed it. (c) The documented fitness cost* reported by Amambua-Ngwa et al., which is the condition under which a post-withdrawal equilibrium is a gradient rather than fixation: the allele is retained where exposure is highest and purged where it is not. If (b) or (c) carries the gradient, it is a drug-exposure or treatment-coverage gradient — higher treatment-seeking and more complete AS-AQ coverage in the south — rather than anything ecological about agro-ecological zones as such. That is testable with drug-pressure covariates joined at the same spatial resolution, and is not tested here.

The previous version reported that Pf8's SnpEff annotation labels the ALT at pfcrt codon 75 as Asp while MalariaGEN calls it Glu, described this as the one marker-naming discrepancy among 23, and credited MalariaGEN with being right on the biology. The diagnosis was wrong. Codon 75 carries two variants — 403621 (A>G, annotated Asn75Asp) and 403623 (T>A, annotated Asn75Lys) — and Asn→Glu requires both, so no single-variant annotation can name N75E at all. The appearance of a discrepancy was created entirely by identifying markers from annotation strings. Reconstructed from the codon, residue 75 is *Glu at 0.071 (n = 1,874)*, exactly matching the other CVIET component residues, and it agrees with MalariaGEN on every one of the 1,874 jointly called isolates. There is no discrepancy to follow a convention about: there is one residue, Glu, and it is ours and MalariaGEN's alike.
